requirement:
A tracked read of an HC GitHub issue node records its identity and a fingerprint
of the supplied title, opening post, and status under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`.
Changing any of those supplied fields changes the fingerprint under the same
fingerprinting rules. The fingerprint excludes cache fetch time and TTL;
refetching otherwise unchanged issue contents does not change it.

The fingerprint describes the issue contents supplied under HC's
[redaction policy](../authoring.md#habeas-req-requirements.authoring.redaction),
including the text presented to an agent.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.inputs` states only observable behavior. I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence, so having no implementation roots is not a gap.

I checked each clause for an implementation choice it prescribes:
- "A tracked read of an HC GitHub issue node records its identity and a fingerprint of the supplied title, opening post, and status". This describes what the observation contains. It names no library, hash algorithm, type, signature or interface. Any code that records the identity plus a fingerprint over those three fields behaves the same. A different hash function or a different internal record layout would still satisfy it.
- "Changing any of those supplied fields changes the fingerprint" and "The fingerprint excludes cache fetch time and TTL; refetching otherwise unchanged issue contents does not change it". These are input/output properties of the fingerprint. A tests or behavioral check can verify them. They do not dictate how the fingerprint is built.
- "The fingerprint describes the issue contents supplied under HC's redaction policy, including the text presented to an agent". This is a requirement on what content is fingerprinted. It does not require a particular mechanism for redaction or delegation.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` is context only. Its obligations are also behavioral: successful reads are included in `Fingerprinted`, a failed read returns an error with no invented observation, and observations are deduplicated by identity and fingerprint. Neither requirement prescribes a structure that an alternative implementation with the same observable behavior would violate.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.inputs`.

**Identity and fingerprint recorded.** `src/sdk/issues.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tracked_issue_status_and_fingerprints_follow_refreshed_redacted_snapshots]` verifies an `OpenIssue` node. It asserts that `first.dependencies()` equals `[Dependency::Node(issue, supplied.fingerprint())]`, so both the node identity and the fingerprint of the supplied content are recorded. The supplied text is parsed to check its name, `title`, `status` and `opening_post` fields.

**Changing title, opening post or status changes the fingerprint.** The test's loop changes `title`, `body` and `state` one at a time on the fake server. Each change is first seen as still fresh before the cache expires. After expiry, `check_inputs(&previous)` is asserted false, with the field name as the assertion message. The loop then re-verifies and checks that the new content contains the new value and that the open/closed output matches the state. This covers every named field. The second test, `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_detects_a_changed_reviewed_issue_body_while_repository_validation_stays_offline]`, shows that a changed body makes a stored issue dependency stale.

**Refetching unchanged contents keeps the fingerprint.** After `expire(dir.path())`, `check_inputs(&first)` is asserted true. The server count rises from 1 to 2, so the content was refetched. The fetch time changes on the refetch, and the fingerprint still matches. This covers the exclusion of fetch time and TTL. The code behind it is `src/sdk/issues.rs#impl[HabeasDomain]/fn[issue_snapshot]`. It fingerprints only a JSON object of title, redacted body and status.

**Redaction.** The body contains a `ghp_…` token. The test asserts that `opening_post` starts with `Wait until ready [REDACTED` and that `supplied.format()` does not contain the token. `supplied.fingerprint()` and `supplied.format()` come from the same prepared content, so the fingerprint describes the redacted text that is presented.

**Not assessed here.** The failed-read behavior (503 returns an error) and the preservation of differing observations belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`, so they are context only.

I found no unmarked relevant tests and no assertion gaps.

The fingerprint describes the issue contents supplied under HC's
including the text presented to an agent.
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
